title: CUMMINSIND_practice › 1.3 Plants `[AR26]`

body:
`thesis:paper-call:CUMMINSIND:q3fy27-opm-17pct-plus` (made 2026-11-21, P = 0.38, base 0.45). Our rules forbid editing a call after it is made. Facts surfaced here that its reasoning did **not** use, recorded for the post-mortem:
- **Q2 FY27 OPM was 15.3%** [506 ÷ 3,301]. It **included an unquantified one-off "true-up" of corporate cost allocations** in other expenses `[CC-Q2FY27]`. Other expenses were 9.66% of sales against 8.34% a year earlier (+₹54 cr). If ₹25–40 cr was the one-off [EST], normalised Q2 OPM ≈ 16.1–16.5%. Reaching 17% then needs only ~0.5–0.9 pp more from pricing and materials.
- **For YES:** pig iron/steel flat to softer in Oct–Nov 2026 `[WEB]`; price hikes "starting" on new orders `[CC-Q2FY27]`; H1 receivables released.
- **For NO:** the inventory layer at high cost (+₹186 cr in H1) flows into Q3 COGS; employee cost +18% YoY is recurring; management refused to call a bottom; order-book execution at old prices.
- Net: the one-off is the most decision-relevant new fact. **Lesson for the paper-call method: read the other-expenses commentary before setting a margin probability.**

body:
1. **Market cap is approximate.** It is built from implied shares in PIT disclosures (holding ≥ 1%) plus a price-basis
   factor. Error is likely ±5–10%, which is fine for ×0.5–×2 matching and for the ₹500–20,000 cr band edges. 52 events were
   lost for lack of a share count or mcap.
2. **Control universe** = companies with any PIT filing in 2020-12 → 2025-01 (≈ all actively traded NSE names). It is not a
   point-in-time NSE equity list. Firms listed after the window (and so absent) cannot be drawn for early dates, a small
   bias.
3. **Skew.** Mean +6%, median −7%. The rule's economic value depends on holding the whole basket, so that the few 3–5×
   winners are captured. A concentrated version (5–10 names) would usually lag.
4. **One regime.** 2021–24 was the strongest Indian small/mid-cap run in a decade. Promoter buyers in metals, capital goods
   and rail rode that wave; part of the +6% may be sector or momentum exposure that size-matching does not remove. No
   sector-matched control was run.
5. **Coverage drift.** NSE PIT row counts halve from 2021 to 2024. If some promoter purchases were disclosed only on BSE
   or under different modes, the event set is incomplete. The magnitude of the drift was not verified.
6. **Costs and impact** are ignored (₹500–2,000 cr names: 0.5–1% round trip plus impact). They would cut the small-cap mean.
7. Index benchmark is NIFTY 500 *price* (no dividends), so the index comparison flatters events by about 1.2%/yr. It is
   context only.

data.section: 5. Credibility-generated forward calls (rule-set probabilities)

title: US-WTS › 5. Credibility-generated forward calls (rule-set probabilities)

body:
- **Small n and mostly pending.** 43 of 82 promises are scored, and every FY2026 item is pending. Refresh after the Q4-2026 calls (late Jan–Feb 2027).
- **Reading depth.** The ledgers come from the Motley Fool takeaway lists, the full CFO outlook sections and targeted greps, not a line-by-line read. Quotes marked [Fool summary] are the transcriber's paraphrase. Four of 24 calls were read from 8-K press releases only, because no Fool transcript was found and guessed URLs returned 404. For Lincoln, that leaves two quarters nearly empty.
- **Single-source outcomes.** Organic growth, adjusted margins, segment figures and adjusted EPS come from the companies' own later calls and releases. GAAP revenue, operating income, EPS, capex, FCF, buybacks and dividends were re-derived from SEC XBRL (second source).
- **A. O. Smith's basis change.** China moved to discontinued operations in Q4-2026. Total-company FY2026 promises made before October are scored *withdrawn* or measured ex-China. The structured revenue call checks that the 10-K comparative is ex-China (~$3,155 mn).
- **Peer medians at 100%.** With three peers that rarely miss, one partly-delivered capex promise moves SAC by 5–10 pts. US SAC values are noisier than India's.
- **Survivorship and selection:** four listed, profitable, dividend-paying firms in a 2025–26 data-centre/price upcycle. A downturn sample would look different.

title: lessons › L9 (2026-11-20) — Method tests are not recommendations

body:
**Business.** KMT (marine transportation; 57% of FY2025 revenue, 75% of segment operating income) moves petrochemicals (48% of marine
revenue), black oil (26%), refined products (23%) and agricultural chemicals (3%) by tank barge `[10K25]`:
- **Inland:** ~80% of marine revenue. Mississippi River System and the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway. 1,105 barges = **28% of the ~4,004-barge
  industry fleet** (FY2025).
- **Coastal:** ~20%. 28 barges and 24 tugs, ~100% under term contracts.

KDS (43% of revenue) is mainly a distributor and packager:
- Engines and power-generation packages (MTU, Cummins, EMD).
- Allison transmissions; on-highway service.
- Marine repair.
- E-frac equipment.

Power generation was ~52% of KDS revenue in Q4-25 and ~46% in Q3-26; the backlog is "north of $1.5bn" with book-to-bill > 1 (Q3-26 call).

**Units:**
1. The **tank barge** (revenue and EBITDA per barge; ton-miles per barge).
2. The **towboat + crew** (horsepower; ~¼ of horsepower is chartered).
3. The **contract** (term 70% / spot 30% of inland revenue in 2025; time charters 59% of term).
4. For KDS, the **OEM franchise territory** and the **power-gen backlog**.

For a widely held US company, the "related party" is management (protocol v1.2).

**Peers:** no listed pure inland tank-barge peer exists (Ingram, ACBL, Canal Barge and Marquette are private). Matson is the nearest Jones Act
comparison (14.5x FY25 EPS). Cummins (OEM, 19.7x) and Generac (power gen; FY25 EPS depressed) are KDS references.

data.section: L9 (2026-11-20) — Method tests are not recommendations

title: lessons › L9 (2026-11-20) — Method tests are not recommendations

body:
1. **Two start dates, one credit cycle.** The 2016 window contains the PSU-bank NPA recognition (AQR), the IL&FS /
   DHFL freeze (2018–19), YES Bank (2020) and the Mar-2020 crash; the 2018 window starts near the PSU trough. The two
   disagree more than their CIs (P(≤0.5x) 42% vs 9%). The pooled number is a cycle average of two points, not a
   stable rate. Recompute when stage 1 gives more start dates (2012, 2014, 2020).
2. **The blow-up price rule counts the Mar-2020 crash** even where the stock recovered (Poonawalla/Magma 2016 and 2018,
   Allahabad 2018, Indian Bank 2018, Bharat Financial 2018, PNB Housing 2018, IDFC 2016, Satin 2018: 8 of 29). The
   "permanent" column (19.6%) is the better anchor for "lost most of the money and never got it back".
3. **Known episodes outside the class:** YES Bank (₹53,500 cr / ₹42,200 cr at T) and Indiabulls Housing (~₹35,000 cr)
   were above the band; PMC Bank and IL&FS Financial Services were never listed (no IL&FS-group listed lender exists);
   Altico, Srei Equipment unlisted. So the class does *not* include the two largest listed lender failures of the period.
4. **Excluded for data:** Syndicate Bank (in band at both T; screener series mis-scaled, ₹30,418 for a ~₹70 stock) —
   its likely outcomes (2016 start poor, 2018 start ~1.3x via Canara) would move nothing much. DHFL has no page of its
   own; screener carries its pre-2021 history on *Piramal Finance Ltd* (bse:544597), so those two rows are DHFL's
   (crash to 0.03x, no price at T+5 → failed). 101 candidates have no page: almost all tiny dead NBFCs plus old codes of
   live banks (Federal, HDFC, ING Vysya); none is a known in-band lender at T.
5. **Name-keyword frame:** a dead lender whose name carries no lender word is missed (live ones are covered by the
   industry map and the explicit list). Size uses rounded market-cap-to-sales (±0.05; 1 row straddles a band edge, plus the 2 overrides).
6. **Price only**: dividends excluded (~1–2%/yr for lenders) → P(≥3x) slightly understated. PSU-bank recapitalisation
   dilution is inside the price, which is correct for a holder.
7. **Classification is today's screener label**, applied backwards (Ujjivan Financial Services, Equitas Holdings and IDFC
   counted as lenders; Edelweiss and JM Financial not).

body:
S H Kelkar's 18.7x trailing P/E included ₹63 cr of fire-insurance gains in ₹159 cr PBT — core P/E ~33–37x. The v1.4 normalised-EPS
check missed it because the 10-yr average happened to agree. **Rules:** compute core EPS (ex-exceptionals, ex-other income, after
interest) before valuation temperature. When ROIIC < cost of equity and net debt is large, DCF value can be below net debt — the
whole EV above 1x is an exit-multiple bet (L21). L42 again: 2/2 draws in this frame family had group ROIC < CoE. SHK missed both
margin numbers and dates → L26's pattern is a tendency, not a law. Check whether promoters vote on their own relatives' re-appointment.
Open: pollution-board scraper (no structured source); chemicals/F&F peer credibility ledger.
